headline: Billionaire investor Peter Thiel said in private lectures that former US president Barack Obama and Pope Leo XIV exploit public fear of AI for popularity.
score_reason: A provocative claim from closely followed figure, reported from recordings, but it is his opinion and the lectures were on 28 Sep and 5 Oct.
importance_line: The row adds a religious and political layer to the AI regulation fight, but Thiel's claims are opinion, Obama and the pope are named only as targets, and no reply was seen.
summary: Politico's Decoded newsletter reports, as relayed by Fortune, that Peter Thiel, co-founder of PayPal and Palantir and a leading tech investor, said in closed-door lectures in Nashville on 28 Sep and 5 Oct 2026 that Barack Obama and Pope Leo XIV exploit AI's unpopularity to boost their own standing, according to recordings it obtained. His remarks respond to Obama's recent call for Democrats to build an AI plan and to the pope's May encyclical on protecting people in the age of AI; Thiel's representatives did not respond to Politico.
notes: inkl page blocked (403); read Fortune's report, which credits Politico's Decoded for the recordings. Reply: Thiel's remarks answer Obama's September fundraiser comments and Pope Leo's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (May 2026), both named by Fortune. 'Co-founder of PayPal and Palantir' is general knowledge, not from the article.
